subject: Biology
owned_sme_text: The cell is the structural and functional unit of all living organisms. The cell theory, formulated by Schleiden and Schwann in 1838-1839 and later refined by Virchow in 1855, states three things: all living organisms are composed of cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and all cells arise from pre-existing cells (omnis cellula e cellula). Cells fall into two broad categories: prokaryotic and eukaryotic. Prokaryotic cells (bacteria, archaea) lack a true membrane-bound nucleus; their genetic material lies free in the cytoplasm as a single circular DNA molecule called the nucleoid. Many prokaryotes also carry smaller circular DNA called plasmids. Prokaryotic cells are typically 1-10 micrometres in size, have 70S ribosomes, lack membrane-bound organelles, and have cell walls made of peptidoglycan (in bacteria) or pseudopeptidoglycan (in archaea). Eukaryotic cells (animals, plants, fungi, protists) have a true membrane-bound nucleus, multiple linear chromosomes, 80S ribosomes (with 70S ribosomes inside mitochondria and chloroplasts — supporting the endosymbiotic theory), and a range of membrane-bound organelles. The plasma membrane is a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins, as described by Singer and Nicolson's fluid mosaic model (1972). Phospholipids have a polar head and two non-polar tails; cholesterol modulates fluidity in animal cell membranes. Integral proteins span the bilayer; peripheral proteins are attached to one face. The cell wall in plant cells is composed primarily of cellulose; in fungi it is chitin; in bacteria it is peptidoglycan. The nucleus, bound by a double membrane perforated by nuclear pores, contains chromatin (DNA + histone proteins) and the nucleolus (site of ribosomal RNA synthesis). Mitochondria are the powerhouse of the cell, sites of aerobic respiration where ATP is generated through oxidative phosphorylation; they have their own DNA and ribosomes. Chloroplasts, found only in plant and algal cells, are the sites of photosynthesis; they too contain their own DNA. The endoplasmic reticulum has two forms: rough ER (studded with ribosomes, makes proteins for export) and smooth ER (lipid synthesis, detoxification). The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins for secretion or for delivery to organelles. Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes for intracellular digestion; they are sometimes called suicide bags because rupture releases enzymes that destroy the cell. The cytoskeleton — microfilaments (actin), intermediate filaments, and microtubules (tubulin) — provides structural support and enables movement. Common NEET traps: confusing 70S vs 80S ribosomes (prokaryotic vs eukaryotic — but mitochondria and chloroplasts inside eukaryotes have 70S!), and confusing the cell-wall composition across the three domains. Refer to NCERT Class 11 Bio Chapter 8 Figures 8.2-8.10 for the standard structural diagrams.
